segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Al-Mu'tasim, however, was glad that Nasr was killed;
and he gave a golden chain to Bashir for his neck.
And in the year 1151
(1151 of the Greeks,
840 of our Lord?), on the ninth of Nisan a red sign appeared in the north.
And there was heavy rain and a flood,
and it caused great devastation in Harran.
And in Haziran there was a violent earthquake in Arzan al-Rum (Erzerum);
and eighteen towers fell from its wall,
and about two hundred souls died.
And in Tammuz a fire broke out in Baghdad and in Basra on the same day and at the same hour;
and more than five thousand shops burned down in Baghdad.
And on that day a certain {OCR?} city in Khorasan was overturned,
and it buried its inhabitants,
and it became a mound of dust.
And after a day, a part of it (of the mound) collapsed {OCR?},
and a man and a donkey came out of it alive.
And on the fourteenth of Elul, an appearance like a cloud was seen in the east;
and it moved towards the north, all the way to the west.
And its upper side was red like blood,
and its lower side was like the appearance of the moon,
such that upon all bodies, walls, ramparts, and houses the light shone the entire night.
At this time, the Romans came by sea to the harbor of Antioch;
and they plundered the merchants and took the people captive.
And al-Mu'tasim ordered, and a fortress was built inside the harbor.
And in the year 1152
(1152 of the Greeks,
841 of our Lord?), Abu Sa'id invaded the land of the Romans and took captives.
And when he departed,
the Romans overtook him in Cilicia,
and they recovered the captives.
And again they invaded,
and they departed in shame.
And the Romans came and took captives from Hadath, Mar'ash, and the region of Melitene.
At this time, Theophilos sent gifts to al-Mu'tasim,
and he requested an exchange of captives with the Arabs.
And al-Mu'tasim accepted the gifts,
and repaid them twofold, saying:
"Our law does not justify equating a Muslim with a Roman.
If you give me the Arabs without demanding anything in return for them,
we are able to repay twofold,
and in everything surpass you."
And they sent back the ambassadors of the Romans with fifty camel-loads of choice gifts,
and there was peace.
And in the year 1153
who was surnamed Abu Harb;
and thirty thousand hungry and naked men joined him.
notes: (1153 of the Greeks, 842 of our Lord?) there rebelled in Palestine a man whose name was Tamim,
